lesson_title: One Salon, Four Factors, and the Person Paid Last
hook_text: In this tiny container salon, four different incomes are being earned — and the boss collects hers LAST.
clip_script: One container salon at the edge of a busy shopping strip — and every factor of production is inside it. The ground it stands on and the water in the basins: natural resources, paid RENT. The two stylists cutting and braiding all day: labour, paid WAGES. The clippers, the dryers, the chairs, the card machine — made things that exist to produce haircuts: CAPITAL, and the loan behind them charges INTEREST. And the person who looked at that strip and thought, people here need a salon — who borrowed, hires, and lies awake when the geyser bursts: the entrepreneur, paid PROFIT. Now watch the month's money. Forty-five thousand rand comes in. Thirteen and a half thousand leaves for shampoo, colour and electricity bought from other businesses — never really the salon's money. What remains, thirty-one and a half thousand, is what the salon ADDED. Stylists take fifteen thousand. Rent four and a half. Interest two and a half. Three and a half set aside because the clippers are dying slowly. That totals twenty-five and a half — so the owner keeps six thousand. Everyone else was paid first, at amounts promised in advance. The owner was paid last, promised nothing. Burst one geyser and that six thousand goes negative while the stylists still get every cent. Carrying that risk is exactly why the owner decides.
visual_style: A bright container salon cutaway like a doll's house; four glowing labels attaching to ground, stylists, clippers and owner; then banknotes sliding into a queue of piles with the owner's small pile forming last.
mood: Warm, hustling, ending on a sharp truth about risk.
pacing: Quick four-beat labelling, then a deliberate slow count of the split, held beat on the final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never confuse interest, profit and dividends again.
